core_methodology: Dejavu method for sim-to-real transfer of reinforcement learning policies using per-decision importance sampling and betting confidence sequences to ensure safety during policy updates
data_sources: Trajectories collected by a safe baseline policy operating in production (real-world environment)
alpha_potential: Potential for developing robust RL-based trading strategies that can safely adapt to changing market conditions while maintaining performance guarantees
title_cn: 具有终身有效性的概率安全仿真到现实迁移
summary_cn: Dejavu方法通过每决策重要性采样和投注置信序列，为强化学习策略在约束马尔可夫决策过程中的仿真到现实迁移提供概率安全保障。该方法可应用于开发自适应交易策略，在保持安全性的同时进行策略更新，对高频交易和投资组合优化具有潜在价值。

title: Open-world Reconstruction-based Classifier with Concept Drift Adaptation
summary: Data stream processing has become central to modern machine learning applications, with concept drifts and novel class appearances posing the primary challenges faced by recognition methods. Adapting to concept drifts while also being able to detect novel classes and distinguish groups of unknown observations can be seen as a step towards effective method employment in an open-world setting. This work proposes a classification method that can detect and learn the distributions of new, unknown classes, as well as adapt to concept drifts once the distribution of known classes shifts. The proposed method uses the autoencoders' reconstruction errors and the KDE that models their distribution. The autoencoders incrementally adapt to the changing distributions of known classes via weight fine-tuning, resulting in continuous adjustment to evolving concepts. Conducted experiments used a diverse set of synthetic data streams, embeddings of a real-world static CIFAR dataset arranged into a stream to simulate concept drifts and the emergence of unknowns, as well as real-world datasets where novelty is observed. The methodology was compared with state-of-the-art approaches with three-criterion recognition quality assessment and resource consumption evaluation. The results indicate that the proposed method is competitive with reference approaches in stationary environments and performs best when concept drifts occur.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a classification method using autoencoders' reconstruction errors and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) to detect and adapt to concept drifts and novel class appearances in data streams. The autoencoders are incrementally fine-tuned to adapt to changing distributions of known classes.
data_sources: The experiments used synthetic data streams, embeddings of the CIFAR dataset arranged to simulate concept drifts, and real-world datasets with observed novelty.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be applied to detect regime changes in financial markets or identify emerging patterns in market data that traditional models might miss. The ability to adapt to concept drifts is particularly relevant for trading strategies that need to adjust to changing market conditions.
title_cn: 基于重构的开放世界分类器与概念漂移适应
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种利用自编码器重构误差和KDE的方法，用于检测和适应数据流中的概念漂移和新类别出现。在量化交易中，该方法可应用于市场状态识别和策略自适应调整，特别是在市场环境快速变化时。

title: Future-Informed Actor-Critic
summary: Actor-critic methods optimize a parametrized policy using a critic to estimate their policy gradient. Recent work has shown that conditioning the critic on features of future states, actions, or rewards can improve sample efficiency and even final return. However, existing methods are restricted to exogenous features (independent of actions), overlooking endogenous features (dependent on actions) that may be crucial for credit assignment. We introduce the future-informed value function, which can be conditioned on both exogenous and endogenous features of future states, actions, and rewards. Then, we express the policy gradient using this value function, yielding the future-informed policy gradient. Building on that, we propose the future-informed actor-critic algorithm. Empirical results show that this algorithm leveraging endogenous features of the future outperforms standard actor-critic algorithms in environments with noisy and sparse rewards.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a future-informed actor-critic algorithm that extends traditional actor-critic methods by conditioning the critic on both exogenous and endogenous features of future states, actions, and rewards. This allows for better credit assignment and improved performance in environments with noisy and sparse rewards.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to various types of financial data, including market prices, order book data, or alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to leverage endogenous features of the future could be valuable for developing trading strategies that require precise credit assignment, such as those dealing with sparse or noisy financial signals. This could be particularly useful in high-frequency trading or portfolio optimization where reward signals are delayed or noisy.
title_cn: 未来信息驱动的行动者-评论家方法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种未来信息驱动的行动者-评论家算法，通过利用未来状态、行动和奖励的内生特征，改进了传统行动者-评论家方法在稀疏和噪声奖励环境中的表现。该方法在量化交易中可能有助于开发更精确的信号分配策略，特别是在高频交易和组合优化中。

title: Optimal Regret for Profit Maximization in Bilateral Trade
summary: Learning to profit from trade requires learning both sides of a market: what a seller is willing to accept and what a buyer is willing to pay. We study repeated bilateral trade, where an intermediary posts a purchase price to a seller and a sale price to a buyer whose valuations are drawn from an unknown joint distribution. Trade occurs only if both parties accept their respective prices, in which case the intermediary earns the difference between the two prices. The intermediary observes only whether trade occurs, without observing either valuation. We show that learning both sides of the market is no harder, in terms of regret, than learning just one. Specifically, we design an algorithm achieving regret $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{2/3})$ against the best fixed pair of prices, matching, up to logarithmic factors, the classical lower bound for one-dimensional dynamic pricing. Our result shows that the classical one-dimensional regret rate survives the transition to two dimensions, raising the question of whether this absence of a curse of dimensionality extends to arbitrarily high dimensions.
core_methodology: The paper presents an algorithm for learning optimal pricing strategies in bilateral trade scenarios where the intermediary only observes trade outcomes (not the underlying valuations). The methodology achieves regret bounds comparable to one-dimensional pricing problems, suggesting efficient learning in two-dimensional settings.
data_sources: Implicitly requires historical trade acceptance/rejection data from bilateral transactions (though not explicitly financial market data, the framework is analogous to dealer markets or OTC trading).
alpha_potential: Potential applications in market-making scenarios where the intermediary needs to simultaneously learn bid/ask spreads from limited observations. The methodology could help optimize dealer pricing in illiquid markets or dark pools where full order book information isn't available.
title_cn: 双边贸易中利润最大化的最优遗憾
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种在仅能观察交易是否达成（无法获知买卖双方实际估值）的双边贸易场景中学习最优定价策略的算法。该成果可应用于做市商策略优化，特别是在流动性不足的市场或暗池交易中，帮助交易商在信息有限的情况下同时学习买卖价差。算法实现了与一维定价问题相当的遗憾边界，表明在二维定价场景中仍能高效学习。

title: Drift-admissibility via Optimal Transport
summary: We introduce structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics for assessing whether empirical time-series dynamics are compatible with a prescribed predictable-drift class. Our approach translates a pathwise property of stochastic processes into a finite-dimensional projection problem over empirical transition laws, encoding admissibility as row-wise moment constraints on local couplings and quantifying deviations via a Kullback--Leibler projection gap $G_{\lambda,k}$. This yields both a principled diagnostic and a scalable Bregman--Dykstra algorithm that retains the efficiency of Sinkhorn-type methods while incorporating structural constraints. Calibrated against a Brownian reference null, $G_{\lambda,k}$ separates process classes that are indistinguishable by second-order statistics alone---including fractional Brownian motion and BSS processes sharing identical Hurst indices---without asymptotic resampling or continuous-time recovery. This positions the method as a general tool for structure-aware model validation of sequential data.
core_methodology: The paper introduces structure-aware optimal transport diagnostics for assessing time-series dynamics against prescribed predictable-drift classes. It translates pathwise properties of stochastic processes into finite-dimensional projection problems over empirical transition laws, using Kullback-Leibler projection gaps for quantification. The method includes a scalable Bregman-Dykstra algorithm that retains the efficiency of Sinkhorn-type methods while incorporating structural constraints.
data_sources: The methodology is applicable to empirical time-series data, which could include financial market prices, returns, or other sequential financial data.
alpha_potential: The approach can help in identifying and validating stochastic process models that are not distinguishable by second-order statistics alone, potentially uncovering hidden patterns or inefficiencies in financial time-series data. This could be useful for model validation and improving the robustness of quantitative trading strategies.
title_cn: 通过最优传输的漂移可容许性
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于最优传输的结构感知诊断方法，用于评估时间序列动态是否符合预设的可预测漂移类别。该方法通过将随机过程的路径属性转化为有限维投影问题，并利用Kullback-Leibler投影间隙进行量化，能够区分仅通过二阶统计量无法区分的随机过程类别。在金融交易中，该方法可用于模型验证和发现隐藏的市场模式，提升量化策略的稳健性。

title: pESTO: Iterative p-greedy kernel regression with risk-driven Early STOpping
summary: Kernel-based greedy algorithms select suitable approximation nodes by minimizing point-wise error indicators, such as the power function; in this context, they are usually referred to as p-greedy approaches. In the presence of noisy data, deterministic criteria may fail, as the discrepancy between the true solution and its estimate is influenced by both approximation error and noise amplification, and the balance between the two is unknown. This study explicitly separates these two contributions, which are governed by the power function and a Lebesgue-type term, respectively. These bounds motivate the use of the Stein's unbiased risk estimator (SURE) as a proxy of the mean squared error, which in turn provides a principled and computable stopping criterion for the number of nodes to select in the p-greedy procedure. Numerical experiments demonstrate that this approach effectively balances deterministic accuracy and statistical noise contributions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an iterative p-greedy kernel regression method with a risk-driven early stopping criterion, using Stein's unbiased risk estimator (SURE) to balance approximation error and noise amplification in noisy data scenarios.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any noisy financial time series data, such as high-frequency trading data or alternative data with measurement errors.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to optimally balance approximation accuracy and noise reduction could improve signal extraction from noisy financial data, potentially enhancing predictive models for asset prices or risk factors.
title_cn: pESTO：基于风险驱动提前停止的迭代p贪婪核回归
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种改进的p贪婪核回归算法，通过Stein无偏风险估计(SURE)实现噪声环境下的最优节点选择。在量化交易中，该方法可有效处理高频数据噪声，提升因子模型的信号提取能力，适用于需要平衡精度与噪声的金融预测场景。

title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
summary: Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion for off-policy evaluation (OPE) that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk without sample splitting. It focuses on neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under specific conditions (Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, etc.).
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but the methodology is applicable to any high-dimensional context where reward models are used, such as trading signals or market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to improve the evaluation of trading strategies by more accurately estimating the out-of-sample performance of reward models without the need for sample splitting, potentially leading to better strategy selection and optimization.
title_cn: 无需样本分割的高维离策略评估：使用Onsager校正
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种无需样本分割的高维离策略评估方法，通过Onsager校正和目标策略加权准则，直接估计全数据奖励模型的样本外风险。该方法适用于固定深度和宽度的神经网络，在特定条件下（如高斯上下文、单索引奖励等）具有理论保证。在量化交易中，该方法可用于更准确地评估交易策略的样本外表现，优化策略选择。

title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
summary: The recently proposed Score-Repellent Monte Carlo (SRMC) method improves MCMC sampling by tilting the target density $\pi$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the factor $\exp(-\alpha\,\theta_n^\top s(x))$, where the score function $s(x) = \nabla_x \log \pi(x)$, and $\theta_n$ is the score average from past samples. However, a single scalar repellence strength $\alpha\ge0$ cannot handle both the steep and the flat directions in anisotropic energy landscapes at once. We introduce \emph{Geometry-Aware SRMC} (GA-SRMC), which generalizes the Euclidean alignment to $\theta^\top M s(x)$ for any symmetric positive-definite matrix $M$. A stochastic-approximation central limit theorem under a trace constraint on $M$ identifies the trace-normalized inverse Fisher $M_{\rm opt}\propto S^{-1}$ as the unique minimizer of the worst-direction covariance bound, elevating the Fisher information $S=\text{Cov}_\pi(s,s)$ from a proposal-side preconditioner (e.g., FisherMALA, natural gradient) to the bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix, with a single online estimate $\widehat S_n$ serving both roles at no additional computational cost. The full-Fisher online metric $M_n$ converges almost surely to $M_{\rm opt}$ and satisfies a CLT, providing a theoretical guarantee for the online implementation of the GA-SRMC framework. On an $8$-target simulation spanning the condition number $\kappa\in[1.3,100]$ and dimension $d\in[2,785]$, GA-SRMC dominates SRMC in ESS by $\boldsymbol{4.3\times}$ on anisotropic Gaussian ($\kappa=100$) and $\boldsymbol{6.8\times}$ on MNIST under the MALA baseline, by $\boldsymbol{16\text{--}32\%}$ on three well-conditioned logistic-regression posteriors, and by up to $\boldsymbol{+48\%}$ under FisherMALA; gains peak on the most anisotropic targets, and posterior-mean MSE is lower than with SRMC in all $16$ full-Fisher implementations.
core_methodology: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo (GA-SRMC) is an advanced MCMC sampling method that improves upon traditional SRMC by using a symmetric positive-definite matrix to handle anisotropic energy landscapes more effectively. It leverages the Fisher information matrix to optimize the repulsion-side matrix, enhancing sampling efficiency in high-dimensional and anisotropic spaces.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but demonstrates the method on synthetic anisotropic Gaussian distributions and MNIST data, suggesting potential applicability to high-dimensional financial data such as asset returns or risk factors.
alpha_potential: GA-SRMC could be valuable in quantitative finance for improving the efficiency of sampling in high-dimensional posterior distributions, such as those encountered in Bayesian portfolio optimization, risk management, or calibration of complex financial models. The method's ability to handle anisotropic distributions more effectively than traditional MCMC methods could lead to more accurate and faster estimations of model parameters or risk metrics.
title_cn: 几何感知的分数排斥蒙特卡洛方法
summary_cn: 本文提出的几何感知分数排斥蒙特卡洛（GA-SRMC）方法通过利用Fisher信息矩阵优化排斥侧矩阵，显著提高了在高维和各向异性分布中的采样效率。该方法在量化金融中具有潜在应用价值，特别是在贝叶斯投资组合优化和复杂金融模型校准中，能够更快速、更准确地估计后验分布。

title: From Images to Signals: Are Large Vision Models Useful for Time Series Analysis?
summary: Transformer-based models have gained increasing attention in time series research, driving interest in Large Language Models (LLMs) and foundation models for time series analysis. As the field moves toward multi-modality, Large Vision Models (LVMs) are emerging as a promising direction. In the past, the effectiveness of Transformer and LLMs in time series has been debated. When it comes to LVMs, a similar question arises: are LVMs truely useful for time series analysis? To address it, we design and conduct the first principled study involving 4 LVMs, 8 imaging methods, 18 datasets and 26 baselines across both high-level (classification) and low-level (forecasting) tasks, with extensive ablation analysis. Our findings indicate LVMs are indeed useful for time series classification but face challenges in forecasting. Although effective, the contemporary best LVM forecasters are limited to specific types of LVMs and imaging methods, exhibit a bias toward forecasting periods, and have limited ability to utilize long look-back windows. We hope our findings could serve as a cornerstone for future research on LVM- and multimodal-based solutions to different time series tasks.
core_methodology: The study evaluates the application of Large Vision Models (LVMs) to time series analysis, specifically comparing 4 LVMs across 8 imaging methods on 18 datasets for both classification and forecasting tasks. The research includes extensive ablation studies to understand model effectiveness.
data_sources: The paper uses 18 diverse datasets for evaluating LVMs, though specific dataset details aren't provided in the abstract. Likely includes standard time series benchmarks.
alpha_potential: For quantitative finance, this research suggests potential for improved time series classification (e.g., pattern recognition in financial time series), though forecasting applications appear limited based on current findings. May help with regime detection or signal classification when adapted to financial data.
title_cn: 从图像到信号：大型视觉模型在时间序列分析中有用吗？
summary_cn: 本研究首次系统评估了大型视觉模型(LVMs)在时间序列分类和预测中的应用。研究发现LVMs在分类任务中表现良好，但在预测方面存在局限性。对于量化交易，该技术可能在金融时间序列模式识别(如市场状态分类)方面具有应用潜力，但直接预测市场表现的能力有限。

title: Caterpillar GNN: Replacing Message Passing with Graph-Level Aggregation
summary: Message-passing graph neural networks (MPGNNs) dominate modern graph learning. Typical efforts enhance MPGNN's expressive power by enriching the adjacency-based aggregation. In contrast, we introduce a graph-level aggregation over walk incidence-based matrices that are constructed to deliberately trade off some expressivity for stronger and more structured inductive bias. This approach allows for gradual scaling between classical message-passing and simpler methods based on walks. Drawing on weighted automata, we ensure our gradual scaling is polynomial-time and avoids the combinatorial explosion of colored walks. Our second result characterizes the expressive power at each scale using homomorphism counts over a hierarchy of generalized caterpillar graphs. Based on these foundations, we propose Caterpillar GNNs that substantially reduce the number of nodes in the hidden layers of the computational graphs on real-world datasets. This gradual reduction does not obstruct learning, enabling a systematic study of lower-order expressivity. We further describe benchmark settings where task-aligned expressivity supports learning.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Caterpillar GNNs, which replace traditional message-passing in graph neural networks with graph-level aggregation over walk incidence-based matrices. This approach allows for a trade-off between expressivity and structured inductive bias, enabling gradual scaling between classical message-passing and simpler walk-based methods. The methodology is grounded in weighted automata to ensure polynomial-time complexity and avoid combinatorial explosion.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial datasets but the methodology is applicable to any graph-structured financial data, such as market correlation networks, transaction networks, or asset-relationship graphs.
alpha_potential: The Caterpillar GNNs could potentially uncover hidden patterns in financial networks by leveraging structured inductive biases and reduced computational complexity. This could be useful for tasks like portfolio optimization, risk assessment, or detecting market anomalies where graph-structured data is prevalent.
title_cn: 毛毛虫图神经网络：用图级聚合替代消息传递
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种新型图神经网络（Caterpillar GNNs），通过基于行走的图级聚合替代传统消息传递，在表达能力和结构化归纳偏置之间取得平衡。这种方法可应用于金融网络分析，如市场相关性建模或投资组合优化，具有降低计算复杂度的优势。

title: Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging for uncertainty quantification of electricity price forecasts
summary: Quantifying the uncertainty of forecasting models is essential to assess and mitigate the risks associated with data-driven decisions, especially in volatile domains such as electricity markets. In this paper, we propose a computationally efficient isotonic variant of Quantile Regression Averaging (QRA), called Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging (iQRA), for generating probabilistic forecasts from ensembles of point forecasts. Building on QRA, we introduce stochastic order constraints as a hyperparameter-free regularization mechanism that reduces computational complexity while maintaining competitive forecast accuracy. We further demonstrate that the same isotonic regularization principle can be applied to the smoothed estimator of QRA. In an extensive forecasting study of two European day-ahead electricity markets, we show that iQRA and its smoothed variant consistently rank among the top state-of-the-art postprocessing methods in terms of reliability and sharpness. It produces well-calibrated prediction intervals, with smoothed iQRA providing superior reliability even when compared against coverage-oriented conformal prediction. We further introduce a battery arbitrage evaluation, showing that the leading probabilistic methods achieve the highest profit per trade and that probabilistic risk control improves the economic value of trading decisions. Isotonic regularization offers a scalable hyperparameter-free variable selection for linear quantile regression, making iQRA attractive for practical decision-support systems in energy markets.
core_methodology: Isotonic Quantile Regression Averaging (iQRA) with stochastic order constraints for generating probabilistic forecasts from ensembles of point forecasts. Includes a smoothed variant for improved reliability.
data_sources: European day-ahead electricity markets (specific markets not named in abstract)
alpha_potential: Potential for improved risk management and arbitrage opportunities in volatile electricity markets through better probabilistic forecasting. Demonstrated economic value in battery arbitrage applications.
title_cn: 用于电力价格预测不确定性量化的等分位数回归平均方法
summary_cn: 本文提出的iQRA方法通过等渗正则化改进分位数回归平均，在电力市场预测中实现了计算高效且准确的概率预测。该方法在电池套利评估中显示出经济价值提升，适用于能源市场的风险管理和交易决策支持系统。

title: End-to-End On-Device Quantization-Aware Training for LLMs at Inference Cost
summary: Quantization reduces the deployment cost of large language models (LLMs). However, post-training quantization (PTQ) cannot fine-tune model parameters and often degrades accuracy in low-bit settings, while quantization-aware training (QAT) requires backpropagation and incurs high memory overhead. We propose ZeroQAT, a zeroth-order QAT framework supporting both weight and activation quantization. By using forward-only gradient estimation, ZeroQAT removes backpropagation and substantially reduces memory and computation while retaining end-to-end optimization benefits. We further introduce a lightweight variant of ZeroQAT for quantized fine-tuning, which freezes and pre-quantizes most parameters to further cut memory usage. Experiments show that ZeroQAT consistently outperforms representative PTQ and QAT baselines while requiring significantly less memory. For example, ZeroQAT enables fine-tuning of a 13B model at extremely low bit-widths (e.g., 2-4 bits) on a single 8GB GPU, and even allows fine-tuning a 6.7B model on a OnePlus 12 smartphone, demonstrating its practicality for end-to-end QAT on resource-limited edge devices.
core_methodology: ZeroQAT is a zeroth-order quantization-aware training framework that uses forward-only gradient estimation to enable efficient quantization of large language models (LLMs) without backpropagation, significantly reducing memory and computation requirements.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on general LLM quantization techniques that could be applied to financial text or time-series data.
alpha_potential: The method could enable more efficient deployment of quantized LLMs for financial applications such as sentiment analysis, news summarization, or predictive modeling on edge devices, potentially reducing latency and costs in real-time trading systems.
title_cn: 端到端设备端量化感知训练：以推理成本实现大语言模型优化
summary_cn: ZeroQAT提出了一种无需反向传播的量化感知训练框架，显著降低大语言模型在边缘设备上的内存和计算需求。该方法可应用于金融领域的实时文本分析和预测建模，提升量化交易系统的部署效率。

title: Outcome-Based RL Provably Leads Transformers to Reason, but Only With the Right Data
summary: Transformers trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL) with outcome-based supervision can spontaneously develop the ability to generate intermediate reasoning steps (Chain-of-Thought). Yet the mechanism by which sparse rewards drive policy gradient to discover such systematic reasoning remains poorly understood. We address this by analyzing the policy gradient dynamics of single-layer linear Transformers on a synthetic graph traversal task that cannot be solved without Chain-of-Thought but admits a simple iterative solution. We prove that despite training solely on final-answer correctness, policy gradient drives the Transformer to converge to a structured, interpretable algorithm that iteratively traverses the graph vertex-by-vertex. We characterize the distributional properties required for this emergence, identifying the critical role of "simple examples": instances requiring fewer reasoning steps. When the training distribution places sufficient mass on these simpler examples, the Transformer learns a generalizable traversal strategy that extrapolates to longer chains; when this mass vanishes, policy gradient learning becomes infeasible. We corroborate our theoretical results through experiments on synthetic data and with real-world language models on mathematical reasoning tasks, validating that our theoretical findings carry over to practical settings.
core_methodology: The paper explores how Transformers trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL) with outcome-based supervision can develop the ability to generate intermediate reasoning steps (Chain-of-Thought) for solving complex tasks. The focus is on proving that policy gradient dynamics can lead to structured, interpretable algorithms that generalize from simple examples to more complex scenarios.
data_sources: Synthetic graph traversal tasks and real-world language models on mathematical reasoning tasks.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to develop trading strategies where the Transformer learns to generate intermediate reasoning steps for complex decision-making processes, such as portfolio optimization or risk management. The ability to generalize from simpler to more complex scenarios aligns well with the need for adaptive trading strategies in dynamic markets.
title_cn: 基于结果的强化学习证明Transformer能够推理，但仅适用于特定数据
summary_cn: 该研究通过强化学习训练Transformer，证明其在稀疏奖励下能够发展出系统性推理能力（Chain-of-Thought）。这一方法可能应用于量化交易中，帮助模型在复杂市场环境中生成中间推理步骤，从而优化交易决策。研究强调了简单示例对模型泛化能力的关键作用，这对开发适应性强的交易策略具有潜在价值。

title: Interpretability-by-Design with Accurate Locally Additive Models and Conditional Feature Effects
summary: Generalized additive models (GAMs) offer high interpretability through independent univariate feature effects but underfit when interactions are present in data. GA$^2$Ms add selected pairwise interactions, which improves accuracy, but sacrifices interpretability. We propose Conditionally Additive Local Models (CALMs), a new model class that narrows this trade-off: it stays close to GAMs in interpretability and close to GA$^2$Ms in accuracy. CALMs allow multiple univariate shape functions per feature, each active in different regions of the input space. These regions are defined independently for each feature as simple logical conditions (thresholds) on the features it interacts with. As a result, effects remain locally additive while varying across subregions to capture interactions. We further propose a principled distillation-based training pipeline that identifies homogeneous regions with limited interactions and fits interpretable shape functions via region-aware backfitting. Experiments on diverse classification and regression tasks show that CALMs never underperform GAMs, often beat them and achieve accuracy broadly comparable to GA$^2$Ms, while preserving the univariate auditability that GA$^2$Ms forfeit.
core_methodology: Conditionally Additive Local Models (CALMs) that allow multiple univariate shape functions per feature, active in different regions of the input space defined by simple logical conditions on interacting features. This approach maintains interpretability while capturing interactions.
data_sources: Not specified in the abstract, but typically applicable to structured financial data such as price series, fundamental data, or alternative data sources.
alpha_potential: CALMs could be useful for developing interpretable trading signals that capture non-linear relationships and interactions in financial data without sacrificing model transparency, which is crucial for risk management and regulatory compliance.
title_cn: 通过精确的局部可加模型和条件特征效应实现可解释性设计
summary_cn: 本文提出的条件可加局部模型（CALMs）在保持广义可加模型（GAMs）高可解释性的同时，通过允许每个特征在不同输入区域具有多个单变量形状函数，有效捕捉特征间的交互作用。这种方法在金融交易策略开发中具有潜在应用价值，特别是需要平衡模型准确性和监管合规要求的场景。

title: EvoAgent: An Evolvable Agent Framework with Skill Learning and Multi-Agent Delegation
summary: This paper proposes EvoAgent--an evolvable large language model (LLM) agent framework that integrates structured skill learning with a hierarchical sub-agent delegation mechanism. EvoAgent models skills as multi-file structured capability units equipped with triggering mechanisms and evolutionary metadata, and is designed to enable continuous skill generation and optimization through a user-feedback-driven closed-loop process. In addition, by incorporating a three-stage skill matching strategy and organizing the agent as a harness whose only self-modified component is a persistent, user-owned state (profile, memory and skills), the framework supports dynamic task decomposition for complex problems and long-term capability accumulation. Experimental results based on real-world foreign trade scenarios demonstrate that, after integrating EvoAgent, GPT-5.2 achieves substantial improvements in professionalism, accuracy, and practical utility. Under a five-dimensional LLM-as-Judge evaluation protocol, the overall average score increases by approximately 28%. Further model transfer experiments indicate that the performance of an agent system depends not only on the intrinsic capabilities of the underlying model, but also on the degree of synergy between the model and the agent architecture. Code and documentation are released at https://github.com/Focus-AI-Center/Mentarc-EvoAgent; the evaluation corpus contains proprietary business data that cannot be released, so the reported results are for reference only.
core_methodology: Evolvable LLM agent framework with structured skill learning and hierarchical sub-agent delegation, featuring continuous skill generation and optimization through user feedback.
data_sources: Proprietary business data from real-world foreign trade scenarios (not publicly available).
alpha_potential: Potential for automating complex financial decision-making processes, improving accuracy and adaptability in trading strategies through dynamic skill evolution and multi-agent collaboration.
title_cn: EvoAgent：一种具有技能学习和多智能体委派机制的可进化智能体框架
summary_cn: EvoAgent提出了一种可进化的大型语言模型智能体框架，通过结构化技能学习和层次化子智能体委派机制，实现了持续的能力优化。在真实外贸场景中验证显示，该系统可显著提升专业性和准确性（平均评分提高28%）。该框架在量化交易中具有应用潜力，可支持复杂金融决策的自动化处理和动态适应。

title: Self-Programmed Execution for Language-Model Agents
summary: At the heart of a language model agent is an orchestrator program which is responsible for the state transition between consecutive turns. In existing systems, this program is implemented in the harness. This paper introduces self-programmed execution (SPE), in which the model completion is itself the orchestrator program, and the harness evaluates this program but does not impose any fixed orchestration policy. Formally, an SPE state of an agentic machine is one from which a model completion can load any successor state up to an embedding, and an instance of an SPE state is one which executes the model completion as a program. In practice, the program requires a language with unusual features, as its source code doubles as the content of the model's context window. I therefore introduce Spell, a Lisp dialect in which programs can edit and re-evaluate themselves, and effectful expressions like model invocations are structured such that re-evaluating an edited program does not replay its side effects. Experiments with existing models, not trained for SPE or Spell, show that frontier models can learn Spell in-context and accomplish challenging agentic tasks. These results demonstrate how an LM can act as an agent without any fixed orchestration policy, and they raise the question of what self-orchestration strategies might be learned by a model trained for self-programmed execution. Code is available at https://github.com/lukejoconnor/spell.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Self-Programmed Execution (SPE), where a language model's completion acts as an orchestrator program for state transitions in agentic systems, using a Lisp dialect called Spell that allows programs to edit and re-evaluate themselves.
data_sources: No specific financial data sources mentioned, but the methodology could theoretically be applied to any data stream used in trading systems.
alpha_potential: Potential lies in dynamic, self-modifying trading strategies that can adapt without fixed orchestration policies, possibly identifying market inefficiencies through adaptive learning.
title_cn: 语言模型代理的自我编程执行
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种自我编程执行（SPE）方法，允许语言模型的补全作为协调程序，结合Spell（一种Lisp方言）实现程序的自我编辑和重新评估。在量化交易中，这种方法有望开发出自适应策略，无需固定的协调政策即可动态调整。

title: Can LLMs Take Retrieved Information with a Grain of Salt?
summary: Large language models have demonstrated impressive retrieval-augmented capabilities. However, a crucial area remains underexplored: their ability to appropriately adapt responses to the certainty of the retrieved information. It is a limitation with real consequences in high-stakes domains like medicine and finance. We evaluate eight LLMs on their context-certainty obedience, measuring how well they adjust responses to match expressed context certainty. Our analysis reveals systematic limitations: LLMs fail to reproduce their prior outputs after observing an uncertain context, respond to expressed certainties in a distorted way, and overrely on complex contexts. To address these, we propose an interaction strategy combining prior reminders (feeding the model's own context-free answer back into the prompt), context-certainty recalibration, and context simplification. This approach reduces obedience errors by 25% on average, without modifying model weights, demonstrating the efficacy of interaction design in enhancing LLM reliability. Our contributions include a principled evaluation metric, empirical insights into LLMs' uncertainty handling, and a portable strategy to improve context-certainty obedience across diverse LLMs.
core_methodology: The paper evaluates LLMs' ability to adjust responses based on the certainty of retrieved information, proposing an interaction strategy that includes prior reminders, context-certainty recalibration, and context simplification to improve reliability.
data_sources: The study uses synthetic or constructed datasets to evaluate LLMs' performance in handling uncertain contexts, rather than real-world financial data.
alpha_potential: The proposed methodology could potentially enhance the reliability of LLMs in processing financial news or reports where certainty levels vary, which might lead to better decision-making in trading strategies.
title_cn: 大型语言模型能否对检索到的信息持保留态度？
summary_cn: 本研究评估了大型语言模型（LLMs）在处理不确定检索信息时的响应能力，并提出了一种交互策略以提升其可靠性。通过结合先前提醒、上下文确定性重新校准和上下文简化，该方法减少了25%的服从错误。在金融领域，这一技术可用于改进对不确定市场信息的处理，从而可能提高交易决策的准确性。

title: Ensemble Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimisation
summary: We study zeroth-order optimisation under context distributional uncertainty, a setting commonly tackled using Bayesian optimisation (BO). A prevailing strategy to make BO more robust to the complex and noisy nature of data is to employ an ensemble as the surrogate model, thereby mitigating the weaknesses of any single model. In this study, we propose a novel algorithm for Ensemble Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimisation that remains computationally tractable while managing continuous context. We obtain theoretical sublinear regret bounds, improving current state-of-the-art results. We show that our method's empirical behaviour aligns with its theoretical guarantees.
core_methodology: Ensemble Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimisation (EDRBO) for zeroth-order optimisation under context distributional uncertainty. The method employs an ensemble of surrogate models to enhance robustness and computational tractability in continuous context settings.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but typically applicable to any noisy financial time series data where Bayesian optimisation is relevant (e.g., parameter tuning for trading strategies).
alpha_potential: Potential for improving parameter optimisation in trading strategies by better handling distributional uncertainty and noise in financial data. Could enhance robustness of quantitative models in changing market regimes.
title_cn: 集成分布鲁棒贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: 本研究提出一种集成分布鲁棒贝叶斯优化算法，通过集成模型增强对复杂噪声数据的鲁棒性，在连续情境下保持计算可行性。该方法可应用于交易策略参数优化，提高模型在不同市场环境下的适应能力。

title: NeuroMAS: Multi-Agent Systems as Neural Networks with Joint Reinforcement Learning
summary: Multi-agent language systems are often built as hand-designed workflows, where agents are assigned semantic roles and communication protocols are specified in advance. We propose NeuroMAS, a framework that treats a multi-agent language system as a trainable and scalable neural-network-like architecture with hidden textual intermediate signals. In NeuroMAS, language-agent nodes are role-free but structure-aware: the topology determines how information can flow, while reward-based training determines how nodes communicate, specialize, and coordinate. This formulation shifts multi-agent design from workflow engineering toward architecture design, where depth, width, connectivity, and growth protocol become scalable sources of capability. We provide a theoretical perspective showing why such modular text-valued computation can be parameter-efficient when tasks admit stable decompositions. Experiments show that NeuroMAS improves over both inference-time collaboration methods and trained baselines, and that its gains are not explained by trainable parameter count alone. We further find that organizational scaling is path-dependent: larger systems can fail when trained from scratch, but become stronger when grown progressively from smaller trained systems. These results suggest that learned multi-agent organization is a promising scaling axis for language-model reasoning and generation.
core_methodology: Neural-network-like architecture for multi-agent systems with joint reinforcement learning, focusing on scalable and trainable architectures for language-agent nodes.
data_sources: Not specified in the abstract, but potentially applicable to textual datasets or structured financial data (e.g., earnings reports, news, social media).
alpha_potential: Could be used for extracting complex market signals from unstructured financial text, considering this framework allows agents to specialize and coordinate, potentially uncovering subtle market inefficiencies.
title_cn: NeuroMAS：作为具有联合强化学习的神经网络的多智能体系统
summary_cn: NeuroMAS通过将多智能体系统视为可训练的神经网络结构，结合强化学习优化节点间的通信和协调。在量化金融中，该框架可应用于分析复杂市场信息流，潜在提升基于文本数据的交易信号生成能力。

title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
summary: Linear attention replaces the unbounded cache of softmax attention with a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing sequence mixing to linear time and decoding to constant memory. The hard part is not just what to forget, but how to edit this compressed memory without scrambling existing associations. Delta-rule models subtract the current read before writing a new value, and Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) sharpens forgetting with channel-wise decay. But the active edit still uses a single scalar gate to control two different things: how much old content to erase on the key side and how much new content to commit on the value side. We introduce Gated DeltaNet-2, which generalizes both Gated DeltaNet and KDA by inheriting adaptive forgetting and channel-wise decay while addressing their shared limitation, the scalar tie between erasing and writing. Gated Delta Rule-2 separates these roles with a channel-wise erase gate b_t and a channel-wise write gate w_t, reducing to KDA when both gates collapse to the same scalar and to Gated DeltaNet when the decay also collapses. We derive a fast-weight update view, a chunkwise WY algorithm with channel-wise decay absorbed into asymmetric erase factors, and a gate-aware backward pass that preserves efficient parallel training. At 1.3B parameters trained on 100B FineWeb-Edu tokens, Gated DeltaNet-2 achieves the strongest overall results among Mamba-2, Gated DeltaNet, KDA, and Mamba-3 variants across language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and retrieval. Its advantage is most pronounced on long-context RULER needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks, where it improves the evaluated multi-key retrieval setting and remains strong in both recurrent and hybrid settings. Code is available at https://github.com/NVlabs/GatedDeltaNet-2.
core_methodology: Gated DeltaNet-2 introduces a novel approach to linear attention mechanisms by decoupling erase and write operations in memory management, using channel-wise gates for more precise control over memory updates. This method enhances the model's ability to handle long-context information efficiently.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the model on language modeling, commonsense reasoning, and retrieval tasks, using the FineWeb-Edu dataset (100B tokens). While not directly financial, the methodology could be adapted to financial time series or alternative data.
alpha_potential: The improved handling of long-context information and efficient memory management could be valuable for developing trading strategies that rely on processing long sequences of market data or news, potentially uncovering subtle patterns or signals that are otherwise hard to capture.

title: LAPLEX: The FFT of Learnable Laplace Kernels
summary: Fast matrix--vector multiplication in deep learning usually comes with a choice: fixed geometry and exact computation, as in the fast Fourier transform (FFT), or adaptive geometry paid for by dense parameters, random features, or low-rank surrogates. To move beyond this trade-off, we introduce LAPLEX, a class of exact, trainable (phased) Laplace-kernel operators. A LAPLEX layer is a typically full-rank dense matrix, implicitly defined by learnable coordinate anchors, with FFT-like scaling. Consequently, it supports trainable matrix-vector operations at vector dimensions up to $10^9$ on modern GPUs. As a neural layer, it yields compact projections and classification heads interpretable as soft, trainable routing models. The same primitive also serves as an efficient Gram operator, enabling high-dimensional covariance models on flattened images of dimension $3 \cdot 10^6$ that preserve visible spatial structure without imposing convolutional bias. These applications reflect a single principle: dense geometry can be learned without storing a dense matrix, which enables data-adaptive global interactions in regimes where ordinary dense layers are out of reach. In this sense, LAPLEX separates expressivity from storage cost: it behaves like a dense trainable matrix, but is represented and applied through a small structured set of parameters. Our code is available at: https://github.com/gmum/laplex.
core_methodology: LAPLEX introduces a class of exact, trainable (phased) Laplace-kernel operators that support FFT-like scaling for matrix-vector operations, enabling high-dimensional covariance models and compact projections.
data_sources: No specific financial data mentioned, but methodology is generalizable to high-dimensional time-series or spatial financial data (e.g., asset price matrices, order book states).
alpha_potential: Potential for creating adaptive covariance models for portfolio optimization or detecting non-linear relationships in high-dimensional market data where conventional methods fail.

title: STEP: Learning STructured Embeddings for Progressive Time Series
summary: We present a novel method for learning interpretable representations of progressive time series, that is, data capturing irreversible state transitions such as degradation or task completion. Our approach uses a self-supervised contrastive objective to learn a low-dimensional latent space whose geometry is itself the interpretation: each observation becomes a point on a manifold anchored between two fixed orthogonal prototype vectors, and a trajectory becomes a path across that manifold. From this structure we read a latent compass, the polar coordinates ({\theta}, r) of the latent vector, in which {\theta} tracks the progression of the underlying state (e.g., from healthy to failed) and r identifies the active mode (e.g., the operating condition), without any proxy labels. We evaluate the approach against the state of the art on diverse domains, including industrial degradation, robotic tasks, and neural activity, validating three key capabilities: (1) end-state prediction, (2) multi-step forecasting, and (3) interpretable phase separation. Our method matches or improves over black-box counterparts on all of these while providing transparency about the underlying mechanisms. A simple linear regressor on top of the latent compass coordinates is competitive with deep architectures, direct quantitative evidence that the underlying state is encoded in a geometrically accessible form.
core_methodology: Self-supervised contrastive learning for interpretable time series embeddings with structured latent space representation
data_sources: Progressive time series data (e.g., industrial degradation, robotic tasks, neural activity) - potential adaptation for financial time series with irreversible state transitions
alpha_potential: Possible applications in regime detection, market state tracking, and predictive modeling of financial time series with non-reversible characteristics (e.g., credit default processes, liquidity drying up)

title: Generalized Intention Modeling in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Modeling an opponent's intent is critical for effective decision-making in non-cooperative, competitive, and general-sum multi-agent reinforcement learning. Existing opponent modeling methods encode intent using an embedding derived from episode information chosen a priori, such as the opponent's next action or a future environment state, and use this to guide the ego-agent's behavior. These approaches assume that the chosen information is universally representative of intent; however, we show empirically that this is not the case as intentions are often task- and environment-dependent. To address this, we introduce a task-adaptive opponent modeling framework that learns a performance-driven mixture of multiple intent representations. We further introduce a new intention representation that maximizes mutual information with the ego-agent's future returns, thereby capturing opponent information that is most directly relevant to performance. Our approach consistently matches or exceeds the performance of state-of-the-art baselines across diverse tasks and yields insights into when and why different opponent modeling strategies succeed.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a task-adaptive opponent modeling framework in multi-agent reinforcement learning that learns a performance-driven mixture of multiple intent representations. It also proposes a new intention representation that maximizes mutual information with the ego-agent's future returns.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any environment where agent interactions can be modeled, including financial markets with multiple participants.
alpha_potential: The approach could be adapted to model competitor behavior in algorithmic trading, potentially uncovering patterns or strategies that are not apparent with traditional methods. The focus on performance-relevant intent modeling could help in predicting market movements based on competitor actions.

title: SDS-LoRA: Overcoming Anisotropic Gradient Scaling in Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) enables efficient adaptation of large pretrained models to downstream tasks by parameterizing weight updates with low-rank matrices. In this paper, we investigate the limitations of the LoRA parameterization from a geometric perspective. Specifically, we show that when a full fine-tuning gradient is backpropagated to the low-rank matrices, it undergoes anisotropic scaling driven by their singular values. We argue that this phenomenon is undesirable because it distorts the full fine-tuning gradient by skewing it toward dominant singular directions while suppressing others. Our analyses demonstrate that anisotropic gradient scaling reduces the effective rank of the low-rank matrices' gradients and fails to provide the best possible alignment between the full fine-tuning gradient and its low-rank approximation in LoRA for arbitrary gradients, thereby exacerbating the gap to full fine-tuning. To address these limitations, we propose a new low-rank parameterization, SDS-LoRA, which Structurally Decouples Singular values from the backward pass. Our method ensures that the full fine-tuning gradient backpropagates only through the orthonormal bases of the low-rank matrices' subspaces, independent of their scales. Convergence analysis demonstrates that while LoRA's convergence rate degrades with the condition number of the low-rank matrices, that of SDS-LoRA remains independent of it. Experimental results across natural language and vision benchmarks show that SDS-LoRA improves loss convergence and reduces the gap to full fine-tuning, significantly enhancing adaptation performance. The code is available at https://github.com/JungHunOh/SDS-LoRA_NeurIPS2026.
core_methodology: The paper proposes SDS-LoRA, a new low-rank parameterization method that structurally decouples singular values from the backward pass to better align with full fine-tuning gradients. This addresses limitations in traditional LoRA by preventing anisotropic gradient scaling.
data_sources: Not specifically mentioned (tested on general natural language and vision benchmarks), but methodology could be applied to financial time series or alternative data for model adaptation.
alpha_potential: Potential application in adapting large pretrained models (e.g., LLMs or transformers) to financial prediction tasks more efficiently while maintaining performance closer to full fine-tuning. Could enhance feature extraction or signal generation from complex market data.

title: A Memory Efficient Unified Algorithm for Online Learning of Linear Dynamical Systems
summary: Motivated by the challenge of stabilizing a general unknown linear dynamical system (LDS) from observations, we study the natural prerequisite of online prediction. Our goal is to achieve sublinear regret with a memory footprint that adapts to the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics rather than the full hidden-state dimension. We focus on the practically central regime of systems with low instability complexity -- eigenvalues outside the real stable interval that do not decay rapidly, together with non-semisimple modes -- potentially embedded in an otherwise stable real spectrum of much higher dimension; we write $k$ for this count. This regime is the primary setting in which stabilization is plausible: we show that many systems with high instability complexity cannot be stabilized without exponentially large controls. Thus, prediction is meaningful for stabilization precisely when the instability complexity is small. Within this regime, we introduce a unified online algorithm that handles every LDS (including non-diagonalizable systems with complex or exploding modes) with a learnable parameter count of $\widetilde{O}(k)$. Finally, we prove a lower bound showing that $k$ is a valid complexity measure: any filter-based predictor needs at least $k$ filters. Experiments corroborate our theory: on a high-dimensional system, our predictor sharply outperforms prior methods at an equal parameter budget.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a unified online algorithm for learning linear dynamical systems (LDS) with a focus on systems with low instability complexity. The algorithm achieves sublinear regret with a memory footprint that adapts to the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics, using a learnable parameter count of O~(k), where k is the count of non-semisimple modes and eigenvalues outside the stable interval.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any time-series data, including financial market data such as price series, order book data, or macroeconomic indicators.
alpha_potential: The algorithm's ability to efficiently learn and predict the behavior of complex dynamical systems could be leveraged to identify and exploit market inefficiencies in high-dimensional financial time series. This could be particularly useful for developing predictive models in algorithmic trading, especially in regimes where traditional methods fail due to high dimensionality or instability.

title: Beyond Bayesian Nash: Learning Minimax-Regret Equilibria for Adversarial Team Games under Asymmetric Information
summary: Adversarial team games (ATGs) with asymmetric information, such as adversarial path-finding, goal search, and reachability games on graphs, require strategies that are robust to hidden opponent types, such as a hidden goal flag, and to deception. Under asymmetric information, deception is seen as strategic shifts in the type distribution such that the omniscient opponent can collude with Nature and condition its play on the observed type. Existing risk-neutral solution concepts, such as Bayesian Nash equilibrium (BNE), are sensitive to distribution shifts, while distributionally robust approaches provide guarantees only within a prescribed ambiguity set. To address these limitations, we introduce Probabilistically Robust Minimax-Regret Equilibrium (PR-MRE), a novel equilibrium concept that combines the distribution-free robustness of minimax-regret reasoning with probabilistic information from a nominal type distribution. PR-MRE minimizes worst-case regret over a high-confidence subset of the type space, providing protection against strategic redistribution of probability mass while avoiding the conservatism of fully distribution-free approaches. We show that, for finite normal-form Bayesian games, approximate PR-MRE computation can be formulated as a robust bilinear program and derive a tractable semidefinite relaxation. We then adapt this relaxation into a novel meta-solver within a robust double-oracle framework, PRMRE-PSRO, enabling population-based learning of approximate PR-MRE strategies via deep reinforcement learning best responses. Experiments on graph-structured adversarial team games demonstrate that PR-MRE discovers strategies with substantially improved worst-case performance across hidden types compared to risk-neutral Bayesian Nash equilibrium solutions, resulting in more robust behavior under strategic distribution shifts.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Probabilistically Robust Minimax-Regret Equilibrium (PR-MRE), a novel equilibrium concept that combines minimax-regret reasoning with probabilistic information from a nominal type distribution. It formulates approximate PR-MRE computation as a robust bilinear program and derives a tractable semidefinite relaxation. The methodology is adapted into a meta-solver within a robust double-oracle framework, PRMRE-PSRO, enabling population-based learning of approximate PR-MRE strategies via deep reinforcement learning best responses.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on graph-structured adversarial team games, which could be analogous to market microstructure or strategic interactions in trading.
alpha_potential: The PR-MRE approach could potentially be adapted to develop robust trading strategies that account for adversarial market conditions and asymmetric information, such as high-frequency trading or market-making scenarios where opponents may have hidden information or engage in deceptive practices.

title: Discretizing Continuous Time Series for Imputation with Masked Diffusion Training
summary: Time series imputation is a crucial area for reliable time series analysis, yet it remains challenging due to the complex temporal dynamics and noise of real-world data. Existing approaches, however, exhibit two limitations: missing and observed values are embedded within the same representation space without explicit structural separation, and continuous diffusion-based methods recover the missing values only through many iterative denoising steps rather than by predicting them directly. To address these, we propose the Masked Diffusion Time-series Imputation Model (MDTIM), which leverages the training paradigm of masked diffusion model for imputation tasks. The [MASK] token is structurally orthogonal to valid observations, and because the corrupted state is the partially observed series itself, the model is trained to predict the missing values directly from the observed ones, naturally aligning both the representation and the learning objective with the imputation task. To bridge the gap between discrete masked diffusion and the continuous, ordinal nature of time series, we further introduce Stochastic Discretization, which maps continuous values to ordinal-aware tokens while preserving continuous dynamics. Our experiments on diverse benchmarks confirm that MDTIM achieves superior robustness and scalability, consistently outperforming state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines across various missing scenarios. Code and project page are available at https://dongbeank.github.io/MDTIM/.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Masked Diffusion Time-series Imputation Model (MDTIM), which uses a masked diffusion training paradigm for time series imputation. It employs Stochastic Discretization to map continuous values to ordinal-aware tokens while preserving continuous dynamics, enabling direct prediction of missing values from observed ones.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but mentions diverse benchmarks, implying potential applicability to financial time series data such as stock prices, trading volumes, or other market indicators.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be valuable for cleaning and imputing missing or noisy financial time series data, which is crucial for accurate backtesting and live trading strategies. Improved imputation can lead to better signal extraction and reduced noise in trading models.

title: AgentGrad: Intervention-guided Prompt Optimization for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) achieve strong performance by employing specialized multiple agents, yet their performance depends on the prompt design of each agent. For MAS prompt optimization, textual gradient methods that guide prompt updates using natural-language feedback have emerged as a leading paradigm. In this paper, we identify limitations in two stages of existing textual gradient approaches: gradient extraction and gradient aggregation. In gradient extraction, previous works select a prompt to update without verifying whether modifying it resolves the failure, and derive gradients without agent-level supervision over the corresponding agent's intermediate output. In gradient aggregation, individual gradients are randomly grouped and concatenated, often mixing unrelated failure modes and producing prompts that fail to generalize. To address these limitations, we propose AgentGrad, a prompt optimization framework for multi-agent systems based on sequential intervention and semantic textual gradient abstraction. For each failure, sequential intervention injects a hint into one agent at a time to identify the target agent whose modification resolves the failure. The modified output of the target agent then serves as agent-level supervision for extracting a fine-grained gradient. Semantic textual gradient abstraction clusters semantically similar gradients to prevent mixing unrelated failure modes, and abstracts each cluster into a generalized gradient that captures the shared corrective pattern. Experimental results show that AgentGrad achieves state-of-the-art performance across five MAS benchmarks while reducing wall-clock optimization time by 2.5 times and optimization cost by 21.8% on average compared to the next-best baselines. Our code is available at https://github.com/mlvlab/AgentGrad.
core_methodology: AgentGrad introduces a prompt optimization framework for multi-agent systems using sequential intervention and semantic textual gradient abstraction. It identifies target agents for modification through sequential hint injection and uses agent-level supervision for fine-grained gradient extraction. Semantic clustering of gradients prevents mixing unrelated failure modes.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but focuses on general multi-agent system benchmarks. Potential applications could use market data, news, or alternative data processed by LLM agents.
alpha_potential: The methodology could enhance multi-agent trading systems by improving prompt design for specialized agents (e.g., for news analysis, order execution, risk management). The intervention-guided approach may help identify and correct specific agent failures in trading workflows.

title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
summary: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) is commonly approached through specialized acquisition functions or scalarization schemes designed to explicitly account for trade-offs among non-preferential objectives. In this work, we show that such complexity might be unnecessary. We propose a framework that extends standard single-objective acquisition functions directly to the multi-objective setting through a hypervolume-based methodology. We further extend hedge strategies for acquisition functions, which are typically used only in single-objective optimization, to the multi-objective regime. Our approach requires minimal modification to existing Bayesian optimization pipelines and avoids the need for bespoke multi-objective formulations. We demonstrate how a broad class of commonly used single-objective acquisition functions and hedge strategies can be adapted in a principled manner to handle multiple objectives, while preserving their intuitive interpretation and computational efficiency. Empirically, we evaluate the proposed methods across a range of synthetic and real-world multi-objective benchmarks. Despite their simplicity, our extensions consistently match or outperform more complex state-of-the-art MOBO methods in terms of optimization performance and sample efficiency. These results suggest that effective multi-objective Bayesian optimization can be achieved by reusing and carefully extending well-established single-objective acquisition strategies, offering a simpler and more flexible alternative to existing approaches.
core_methodology: Extends single-objective Bayesian optimization acquisition functions to multi-objective settings using hypervolume-based methodology, and adapts hedge strategies for acquisition functions to multi-objective optimization.
data_sources: Synthetic and real-world multi-objective benchmarks (not specifically financial data).
alpha_potential: Potential application in portfolio optimization where multiple objectives (e.g., risk, return, transaction costs) need to be balanced. The method's efficiency could help in dynamic asset allocation strategies.

title: HarnessNet: Feedback-driven Hierarchical Joint Harness Evolution for Multi-agent Systems
summary: AI agents can evolve by using environment feedback to revise their harnesses, the software managing model inputs, tool use, memory, and execution, while keeping foundation models frozen. Existing studies focus on single agents, leaving joint harness evolution in multi-agent systems (MAS) underexplored. A single global optimizer faces growing context and workload as the system scales, while access restrictions may prevent sharing agent internals or system-wide feedback. We propose HarnessNet, a framework for hierarchical harness evolution in MAS. Its basic unit, Agentron, comprises an evolvable forward harness, a foundation model, and a local optimizer that can observe and modify only that harness. Agentrons form a layered graph through which environment feedback propagates backward, with upstream optimizers receiving node-specific feedback from the downstream layer. This decomposes joint harness evolution into smaller, coordinated tasks with separate contexts, reducing individual optimizers' context and workload while keeping access local. Optimizers need not access all agent trajectories or raw environment feedback. Experiments on AgentBench with multiple foundation models demonstrate the feasibility of training HarnessNet. Compared with a single global optimizer, HarnessNet achieves comparable performance gains while respecting local privacy and requiring fewer tokens and less time per optimizer call. A migration study shows that the evolved harnesses remain jointly effective after replacing the foundation models, suggesting transferability across models.
core_methodology: Hierarchical harness evolution for multi-agent systems where each agent's harness is optimized locally while receiving feedback from downstream layers
data_sources: Simulated environments (AgentBench), no explicit market data used
alpha_potential: Potential application in optimizing multi-agent trading systems where different agents handle distinct market signals or execution tasks, possibly improving coordination and reducing computational overhead

title: Structural Conditional Independence Test via Neural Quantile Resolution
summary: Conditional independence testing is difficult when dependence is weak, localized, or expressed through distributional changes rather than a global mean shift. Existing tests usually return a scalar statistic or p-value, which can detect rejection but gives limited resolution about where the conditional law changes. We propose QRCIT, a quantile-resolution conditional independence test that compares P(X | Z) and P(X | Y, Z) through an amortized quantile deformation. A lightweight residual quantile-flow model first learns the baseline conditional quantile law and then learns the additional deformation induced by Y, yielding both a calibrated global test statistic and an inspectable deformation field over context and quantile level. We also introduce the Structural Dependency Benchmark (SDB), which evaluates real-world-inspired dependence structures, such as context-local, tail-only, sign-reversing, moving-ridge, and mean-neutral patterns. Across synthetic PNL and SDB benchmarks, QRCIT improves detection of structured alternatives while maintaining empirical Type-I control. Increasing quantile resolution consistently improves merged-SDB power, and the local-rescue strategy sharpens detection when dependence is concentrated in structural regions. On Sachs, METABRIC breast cancer, and CCLE/PLX4720, QRCIT provides competitive real-data performance and interpretable deformation patterns. These results support quantile-resolved conditional-law deformation as a practical framework for testing and diagnosing structured conditional dependence.
core_methodology: The paper proposes QRCIT, a quantile-resolution conditional independence test that compares conditional distributions P(X | Z) and P(X | Y, Z) through an amortized quantile deformation. It uses a lightweight residual quantile-flow model to learn baseline conditional quantile laws and additional deformations induced by Y, providing both a global test statistic and an inspectable deformation field over context and quantile level.
data_sources: The paper evaluates the method on synthetic PNL benchmarks, the Structural Dependency Benchmark (SDB), and real-world datasets including Sachs, METABRIC breast cancer, and CCLE/PLX4720. While not financial data, the methodology is transferable to financial time series and cross-sectional data.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to detect structured conditional dependencies (e.g., context-local, tail-only, sign-reversing patterns) could be valuable for identifying non-linear relationships and regime changes in financial markets. The quantile-resolution approach may help uncover alpha in tail events or conditional relationships that standard mean-based tests miss.

summary_cn: 该研究提出的QRCIT方法通过分位数变形检测条件独立性，可识别金融市场中的非线性依赖和尾部关系。其分位数分辨率方法特别适用于检测市场机制变化和极端事件中的条件依赖模式，为量化策略开发提供新的统计工具。

title: Provably Efficient Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDPs
summary: We study representation learning in low-rank Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs), where both value and reward functions are approximated by a set of unknown representation vectors, and the transition dynamics admit a low-rank factorization. The objective is to maximize expected cumulative rewards while complying with constraints on the expected cumulative utility. To achieve this, we propose \texttt{MFRLC} (Model-Free Representation Learning for Low-Rank CMDP), a model-free algorithm that uses a primal-dual scheme to effectively balance reward regret and constraint violations. To the best of our knowledge, \texttt{MFRLC} is the first representation-learning method for low-rank CMDPs that combines the Least-Squares Value Iteration with Upper Confidence Bound (LSVI-UCB) and primal-dual techniques. \texttt{MFRLC} further enhances value function estimation with bonuses for function approximation and learns the mapping from representations to value functions directly, avoiding explicit estimation of the transition kernel. We prove that, with high probability, \texttt{MFRLC} achieves $\widetilde O(K^{3/4})$ reward regret and cumulative constraint violation over $K$ deployment rounds, independent of the size of the state space. To our knowledge, these are the first sublinear regret and violation guarantees for CMDPs with unknown features.
core_methodology: Model-Free Representation Learning combined with Least-Squares Value Iteration and Upper Confidence Bound (LSVI-UCB), using a primal-dual approach to balance reward maximization and constraint satisfaction in low-rank Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs).
data_sources: Generic state spaces with low-rank transition dynamics (not explicitly financial data, but applicable to portfolio states or market regimes).
alpha_potential: Potential for constrained portfolio optimization problems where both returns and risk/utility constraints need to be optimized under uncertainty. The representation learning aspect could help discover latent market regimes or factors.
title_cn: 低秩约束马尔可夫决策过程中的高效表征学习证明
summary_cn: 该研究提出的MFRLC算法通过模型无关的表征学习和对偶技术，在低秩约束MDP中实现奖励与约束的平衡。对量化交易的核心价值在于：1) 适合处理有约束的组合优化问题 2) 表征学习可发现潜在市场状态 3) 无需显式估计转移矩阵，适合高维金融数据。特别适用于需同时优化收益和风险约束的多阶段投资决策问题。

title: Identifying Drift, Diffusion, and Causal Structure from Temporal Snapshots
summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are a fundamental tool for modelling dynamic processes, including gene regulatory networks (GRNs), contaminant transport, financial markets, and image generation. However, learning the underlying SDE from data is a challenging task, especially if individual trajectories are not observable. Motivated by burgeoning research in single-cell datasets, we present the first comprehensive approach for jointly identifying the drift and diffusion of an SDE from its temporal marginals. Assuming linear drift and additive diffusion, we show that non-identifiability can only arise if the initial distribution possesses generalized rotational symmetries. We further prove that even if this condition holds, the drift and diffusion can almost always be recovered from the marginals. Additionally, we show that the causal graph of any SDE with additive diffusion can be recovered from the identified SDE parameters. To complement this theory, we adapt entropy-regularized optimal transport to handle anisotropic diffusion and introduce APPEX (Alternating Projection Parameter Estimation from $X_0$), an iterative algorithm designed to estimate the drift, diffusion, and causal graph of an additive noise SDE, solely from temporal marginals, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated data from linear additive noise SDEs.
core_methodology: The paper presents a method for identifying the drift and diffusion terms of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) from temporal marginals, using an iterative algorithm called APPEX. It assumes linear drift and additive diffusion, and leverages entropy-regularized optimal transport adapted for anisotropic diffusion.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on simulated data from linear additive noise SDEs, but is theoretically applicable to any time-series data, including financial market data.
alpha_potential: The ability to accurately estimate SDE parameters from temporal snapshots could enhance modeling of financial time series, potentially improving volatility estimation, risk management, and derivative pricing strategies. The causal graph recovery aspect might help in understanding market microstructure relationships.
title_cn: 从时间快照中识别漂移、扩散和因果结构
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种从时间边际数据中联合估计随机微分方程漂移和扩散项的新方法，适用于线性漂移和加性噪声情况。对于量化金融，该方法可改进金融时间序列建模，增强波动率预测和因果关系分析能力，但需针对市场数据特性进行适配。

title: Linear Bandits on Ellipsoids: Minimax Optimal Algorithms
summary: We consider linear stochastic bandits where the set of actions is an ellipsoid. We provide the first known minimax optimal algorithm for this problem. We first derive a novel information-theoretic lower bound on the regret of any algorithm, which must be at least $\Omega(\min(d \sigma \sqrt{T} + d \|\theta\|_{A}, \|\theta\|_{A} T))$ where $d$ is the dimension, $T$ the time horizon, $\sigma^2$ the noise variance, $A$ a matrix defining the set of actions and $\theta$ the vector of unknown parameters. We then provide an algorithm whose regret matches this bound to a multiplicative universal constant. The algorithm is non-classical in the sense that it is not optimistic, and it is not a sampling algorithm. The main idea is to combine a novel sequential procedure to estimate $\|\theta\|$, followed by an explore-and-commit strategy informed by this estimate. The algorithm is highly computationally efficient, and a run requires only time $O(dT + d^2 \log(T/d) + d^3)$ and memory $O(d^2)$, in contrast with known optimistic algorithms, which are not implementable in polynomial time. We go beyond minimax optimality and show that our algorithm is locally asymptotically minimax optimal, a much stronger notion of optimality. We further provide numerical experiments to illustrate our theoretical findings.
core_methodology: The paper presents a minimax optimal algorithm for linear stochastic bandits where the action set is an ellipsoid. The approach combines a novel sequential procedure to estimate the parameter norm, followed by an explore-and-commit strategy. The algorithm is computationally efficient, requiring only polynomial time and memory.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is applicable to any scenario where actions can be represented as points in an ellipsoid, which could include portfolio weights or trading signals in financial contexts.
alpha_potential: The algorithm's ability to efficiently explore and exploit in high-dimensional spaces could be valuable for portfolio optimization or adaptive trading strategies where the action space is constrained (e.g., risk budgets). The minimax optimality suggests robustness in adversarial market conditions.
title_cn: 椭球上的线性赌博机：极小极大最优算法
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种在椭球动作集上的线性随机赌博机问题的极小极大最优算法。该方法通过结合参数范数的序贯估计和探索-提交策略，实现了计算高效的高维空间探索。在量化交易中，该算法可应用于受约束的投资组合优化或自适应交易策略，特别是在需要处理高维动作空间和对抗性市场条件时。

title: Differentiable Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
summary: The efficient computation of parametric solution sensitivities is a key challenge in the integration of learning-enhanced methods with nonlinear model predictive control, as their availability is crucial for many learning algorithms.
